text:
sam: FYI build failed on prod linkcheck after merging the perf cleanup PR. Failing fragment: /tutorials/deploy#auto-scaling-behavior. Locally I can see the heading, but the generated slug differs.

leila: Could be non-printing chars from the markdown editor or a carriage return sneaking into the heading. We saw the same when converting from mkdocs.

dmitri: Repro steps I used:

```bash
yarn docs:linkcheck --site=prod 
# then compare slugs for that page
node ./scripts/extract-headings.js docs/tutorials/deploy.md > /tmp/headings.txt
node ./scripts/docusaurus-slugify.js /tmp/headings.txt > /tmp/docusaurus-slugs.txt
node ./scripts/legacy-slugify.js /tmp/headings.txt > /tmp/legacy-slugs.txt
diff -u /tmp/legacy-slugs.txt /tmp/docusaurus-slugs.txt || true
```

I see the legacy slug has "auto-scalingbehavior" (no hyphen) while Docusaurus has "auto-scaling-behavior". There's also a soft hyphen (U+00AD) in the source after "auto-".

sam: Nice catch. How did the soft hyphen get in there? Editor paste?

leila: Likely from a wrapped sentence that was copy-pasted from Google Docs or a word processor. Small but nasty.

sam: Proposed fixes:
- strip soft hyphen / ZW chars as a migration post-pass
- generate redirects from legacy slugs to new slugs
- add a tiny CI job that runs both slugifiers against all headings and fails if mismatches > 0

dmitri: Agreed. I can add a script that emits redirect mappings in the format we use for redirects.js. Example mapping:

```js
module.exports = [
  { from: '/tutorials/deploy#autoscalingbehavior', to: '/tutorials/deploy#auto-scaling-behavior' }
];
```

leila: We should also add a unit test that inserts a soft-hyphen into a heading string and asserts both slugifiers produce the same output after normalization. Keeps regression risk low.

sam: I'll open a small PR with:
1) scripts/migrate/normalize-headings.js (strip U+00AD U+200C U+200B U+FEFF)
2) docs-ci job docs:slug-compare that runs on PRs touching docs/*
3) generate-redirects step for affected migrated pages

docs-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5488 by sam — add heading normalization + slug-compare CI job

dmitri: One caveat: redirects increase redirect table size. If we generate a bunch, let's batch them into grouped redirect rules where safe. Also we should only generate redirects for public-facing fragments referenced externally (we have a small lookup of inbound links).

leila: Good point. We have an inbound-links csv from the old site — we can cross-check and only emit redirects for anchors that have hits. I can add that filter in the generate-redirects script.

sam: OK I'll wire the filter and add a short note in the PR description for docs-platform reviewers. If anyone sees other weird anchors (especially pages converted from mkdocs), paste them here.

deploy-bot: Docs CI (slug-compare) queued. Rerun required after PR merge.
